issue.title: gcal sync -n with -D drops the synced day: sync_args_read_last_n_days_aliases_and_default_to_none fails on master
issue.description:
`native::gcal::cli::tests::sync_args_read_last_n_days_aliases_and_default_to_none` fails on master (observed locally at b04120b0 and in the master CI run for 92b52e4f, run 43285282980).

The combined-flags case asserts that `bob gcal sync -n 3 -D tomorrow` yields `days == ["today", "tomorrow"]`, but `SyncArgs::from_matches` now returns `["tomorrow"]` only:

```
panicked at src/native/gcal/cli.rs:865:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: ["tomorrow"]
 right: ["today", "tomorrow"]
```

The breakage comes from the recent gcal multi-day sync chain (4ed4fdab "support batched multi-day sync", d71a3bf9 "sync the last N days", 4f7ab37f "include synced day in human output"). Either the product contract changed (an explicit `-D` list no longer implies today when combined with `-n`) and the test is stale, or `-n`+`-D` genuinely dropped the synced day, which would be user-visible (a `-n 3 -D tomorrow` sync skipping today). The fix needs to decide which contract is right and align code, test, and docs/gcal.md.

Discovered while investigating record capture bugs; unrelated to that surface but it keeps master CI red alongside the record-fixture failures, so the release train stays blocked until both are fixed.
